title: Judge a representation by the bytes it stops moving
subtitle: Rewriting an acceptance gate that kept rejecting good compression, and what it bought at 128K tokens

stats.label: the per-tile speed rule I had set, withdrawn after a false rejection
bitwise cells for the hybrid route against its own reference
context sizes measured where the hybrid tier decoded faster

lede: Once a model's history lives in host memory, every decode step is bound by how many bytes cross the bus, and the attention kernel's speed is a rounding error. My acceptance gate for compressed history formats did not know that. It measured kernel speed per tile and kept rejecting candidates that would have won. I rewrote the gate around end-to-end economics at the target context size: bytes saved per token against GPU time added. ActiveKV stages a context's attention history across PCIe on each step. At long contexts the copy dominates. A planning analysis for the exact tier put the transfer at many times the cost of the attention itself at 128K.
quote: A format that loses at 8K and wins at 128K is a format for long contexts, and the gate should say so.
evidence: KV-cache offload for LLM inference: an acceptance gate rewritten from per-tile kernel cost to whole-step economics, bytes saved per token against GPU time added.
Performance modelling: a transfer model built from measured bus behaviour on the card, judging each candidate representation at its target context size.
LLM quantization (INT8 KV cache): a compressed history tier that passed 12 of 12 bitwise cells against its own reference and decoded faster at 3 of 3 context sizes.
Engineering judgment: withdrew my own 0.7x per-tile speed rule after it produced a false rejection at 128K tokens.
author: Corey James
